findings.title: Server-only BETTER_AUTH_SECRET can be embedded in the public mobile bundle via an EXPO_PUBLIC_* variable
findings.why_it_matters: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is a server-side signing secret used by Better Auth / Convex. If it reaches the mobile JS bundle, anyone who extracts the APK/IPA can read it and use it to forge sessions or tamper with authentication.
findings.evidence: `readEnv()` maps `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_BETTER_AUTH_SECRET_STUB` into the `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` slot consumed by `@crm/config`'s `parseEnv()`. `mobileEnv()` caches the returned `Env` object and returns it on every call. Expo SDK 53 inlines every `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` variable into the bundle at build time. Even though the mobile client never reads `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, the validated object still carries it, so a developer who accidentally copies the real secret into `EXPO_PUBLIC_BETTER_AUTH_SECRET_STUB` would ship it in the public binary.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not read any `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` variable into `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`. Refactor the mobile env to omit `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` entirely, or use a client-only schema variant in `@crm/config` that does not require server-only secrets. If a stub is still needed to satisfy the shared schema, hardcode a literal such as `'not-used'` directly instead of reading from `process.env`.

findings.title: Sign-out silently ignores secure-storage deletion failures, potentially leaving session tokens on device
findings.why_it_matters: Sign-out must reliably terminate the session on the device. If the session cookie and Better Auth session data survive a sign-out, a later device unlock or app cold start can silently re-authenticate the previously signed-out user, exposing CRM data to a thief or secondary user.
findings.evidence: `clearSecureAuthStorage()` loops over `SECURE_KEYS` and calls `SecureStore.deleteItem(key, SECURE_OPTIONS)` inside an empty `catch {}`. If the iOS Keychain or Android Keystore is locked/unavailable, the exception is swallowed and the function returns normally. `AuthProvider.signOut()` (auth-provider.tsx:133) calls `clearSecureAuthStorage()` inside a `finally` block and immediately dispatches `SIGN_OUT_COMPLETE`, so the UI treats sign-out as successful regardless of whether the data was actually removed.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `clearSecureAuthStorage()` return a success/failure status or throw on failure. In `AuthProvider.signOut()`, do not complete sign-out until deletion is confirmed; surface an error to the user and retry when the keystore is unavailable. As a defensive fallback, overwrite the stored values with an empty string if deletion fails.

findings.title: User-controlled invoice ID is passed to the backend without visible ownership guard, risking IDOR
findings.why_it_matters: Invoice detail contains customer names, line items, amounts, notes, and internal notes — sensitive PII and financial data. If the backend query trusts the client-supplied id without verifying organization ownership, any authenticated user who guesses or iterates invoice ids can read another organization's invoices.
findings.evidence: `useLocalSearchParams()` returns `id` from the route/URL. The screen casts it to `Id<'invoices'>` and passes it directly to `api.invoices.getById` (line 41). The backend implementation of `api.invoices.getById` is not in this diff, so the org-scoped authorization check cannot be confirmed. The query uses `createAuthQuery()`, which authenticates the caller but does not by itself enforce that the resource belongs to the caller's active organization.
findings.suggested_fix: Audit `api.invoices.getById` to ensure it filters by `ctx.user.activeOrganization.id` (or equivalent) and returns only invoices owned by that organization. Add backend integration tests that verify user A cannot fetch invoice ids belonging to user B or another organization. On the client, avoid the `as Id<...>` cast and rely on Convex's generated Id typing.

findings.title: Local `.env` files are not excluded from the EAS build upload
findings.why_it_matters: EAS Build creates a context tarball of the project and uploads it to Expo's build servers. If local `.env` files containing secrets (EXPO_TOKEN, database URLs, Better Auth secrets, etc.) exist in the workspace, they may be included in that tarball and exposed to the build environment even when they are gitignored.
findings.evidence: `.easignore` excludes node_modules, build outputs, docs, design artifacts, and version-control metadata, but it does not contain any `**/.env*` or `**/.env.local*` patterns. The README correctly directs users to use EAS secrets instead of committed values, but the ignore file itself does not close the door on accidental local secret uploads.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit exclusions to `.easignore`: `**/.env*`, `**/.env.local*`, `**/.env.*.local`, `**/credentials.json`, and any other local secret files. Document that production secrets must be created via `eas secret:create` and never placed in files.

findings.title: Environment schema does not enforce HTTPS for production auth/backend URLs
findings.why_it_matters: Email/password sign-in sends credentials to `SITE_URL`. A production build misconfigured with an `http://` URL would transmit those credentials in plaintext, allowing network-level credential theft. The shared env schema is the natural place to prevent this class of misconfiguration.
findings.evidence: `CONVEX_URL`, `CONVEX_SITE_URL`, and `SITE_URL` are validated only with `z.string().min(1)` (plus defaults to `http://localhost:3005`). There is no refine requiring `https://` when `NODE_ENV` is `production` or rejecting non-local `http://` values. `AuthProvider` sets `authClient` `baseURL` to `mobileEnv().SITE_URL`, and `signIn.email()` sends the password there.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Zod refine (or a separate client schema) that requires `CONVEX_URL` and `SITE_URL` to start with `https://` when `NODE_ENV === 'production'`, while continuing to allow `http://localhost` for development. Reject any production URL that is not HTTPS.

residual_risks.title: Exported `readSecureValue` helper exposes a raw token read primitive
residual_risks.description: `readSecureValue` is exported and can read the Better Auth session cookie or session data. No code in the diff uses it. If a future feature or debugging snippet logs its result, session tokens could be written to logs or crash reports. Consider removing the export or gating it behind a debug-only build flag.

residual_risks.title: Convex auth is not cleared immediately on TOKEN_REVOKED
residual_risks.description: When `useSession` reports an error, the provider clears secure storage and dispatches `TOKEN_REVOKED`, but it does not call `convexClient.clearAuth()`. The existing Convex WebSocket connection may remain authenticated until the current JWT expires, leaving a short window where revoked sessions can still read data.

residual_risks.title: Error boundary surfaces raw error messages to users
residual_risks.description: The boundary renders `error.message` directly. If backend errors ever include internal ids, stack traces, or other sensitive metadata, this would expose them in the UI. Today the messages appear generic, but this is a brittle control.

residual_risks.title: No certificate pinning or root/jailbreak detection
residual_risks.description: The MVP relies on the device certificate store for TLS. There is no pinning of the Convex/Better Auth server certificates, and no detection of compromised devices. This is acceptable for an internal MVP but should be revisited before public store release.

testing_gaps: Extract a release APK/IPA and grep its JS bundle for `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` and the value of `EXPO_PUBLIC_BETTER_AUTH_SECRET_STUB`; confirm no real server secret is present.

Unit-test `clearSecureAuthStorage()` with mocked `SecureStore.deleteItem()` failures; verify `AuthProvider.signOut()` does not report success and does not dispatch `SIGN_OUT_COMPLETE` while tokens remain.
Backend integration test for `api.invoices.getById`: user A attempts to fetch an invoice id belonging to another organization; expect UNAUTHORIZED/NOT_FOUND.
Inspect the EAS build context tarball (or run a local EAS build) and confirm no `.env`, `.env.local`, or `credentials.json` files are uploaded.
Schema test: assert that production inputs with `http://` URLs for `SITE_URL` or `CONVEX_URL` fail validation, while `http://localhost` development inputs pass.
End-to-end token revocation test: revoke the session server-side while the mobile app is foregrounded and verify Convex queries stop returning data immediately (or within the current JWT TTL).
